text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, you should create clear and consistent endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is essential because it helps other developers understand how to use your API quickly. You should also plan for versioning from the start. This allows you to improve your API without breaking existing applications that depend on it. By following these practices, you make your API reliable and friendly for everyone.
